title: CT 105 (download-client): route it through the AirVPN WireGuard tunnel with a kill-switch
description:
Operator decision 2026-10-11: the download client's traffic goes only through AirVPN; if the tunnel is down, nothing leaves on the home connection (a kill-switch).

Measured 2026-10-11: CT 105 (download-client, 192.168.1.24) has no VPN — interfaces lo and eth0 only, no /etc/wireguard, no wg-quick unit, default route via 192.168.1.1, and a global IPv6 address; qBittorrent (qbittorrent-nox.service, Web UI on 8080, torrent port 61661) sends its traffic on the home connection (public IPv4 67.240.32.243). The AirVPN WireGuard config is stored in the engine as the secret AIRVPN_WG_CONF (Switzerland, ch3 entry3, UDP 1637). CT 105 is unprivileged (features: nesting=1).

Inside CT 105: install wireguard-tools, write the stored AirVPN config ($AIRVPN_WG_CONF, never as a literal) to /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf with mode 600, and bring it up with wg-quick at boot (wg-quick@wg0, enabled). Add a kill-switch in the container's own firewall so that, apart from the LAN (192.168.1.0/24 — the Web UI on 8080 stays reachable from home) and the VPN endpoint itself, no IPv4 or IPv6 traffic leaves through eth0; it must persist across reboots. If WireGuard cannot create its interface inside this unprivileged container, say so with the error and stop.

Operator review 2026-10-11 of the drafted block: This draft dropped the step's work: it only installs packages. Keep the whole step: (1) write the tunnel config from the HOST, as its own command after the packages are installed and before wg-quick runs — pct exec 105 -- sh -c 'umask 077; mkdir -p /etc/wireguard; cat > /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf' <<< "$AIRVPN_WG_CONF" — never inside the in-container script (the runner does not send the secret there); (2) install resolvconf (or openresolv) too, because wg-quick needs it when the config has a DNS line; (3) enable wg-quick@wg0 at boot and bring it up; (4) the kill-switch as in the earlier draft: iptables and ip6tables OUTPUT dropping everything on eth0 except the LAN 192.168.1.0/24 and the WireGuard endpoint port, INPUT allowing the Web UI 8080 from the LAN, persisted with a restore unit. If wg-quick fails inside this unprivileged container (for example setting net.ipv4.conf.all.src_valid_mark), stop and say so with the error.

Operator review 2026-10-11 of the drafted block: Two drafts in a row carried only the package install. The in-container commands must be these, in this order (the config file is already written from the host by SECRET_FILES; `ip6tables` is part of the iptables package, not a package of its own): `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v4 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v6 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `apt-get install -y wireguard-tools resolvconf iptables iptables-persistent`; `chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf`; `iptables -F OUTPUT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p udp --dport 1637 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `ip6tables -F OUTPUT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d fe80::/10 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `netfilter-persistent save`; `systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0`. If `wg-quick` fails (for example setting net.ipv4.conf.all.src_valid_mark inside this unprivileged container), stop and report the error — the kill-switch is already in place, so nothing leaks.

Operator review 2026-10-11 of the drafted block (supersedes the earlier command list): the last run's apt install failed — stale package lists (404) and wireguard-tools pulling a linux-image Recommends a container cannot use. The in-container commands are these, in this order (wg0.conf is written from the host by SECRET_FILES): `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v4 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v6 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `apt-get update`; `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends wireguard-tools resolvconf iptables iptables-persistent`; `chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf`; `iptables -F OUTPUT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p udp --dport 1637 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `ip6tables -F OUTPUT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d fe80::/10 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `netfilter-persistent save`; `systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0`.

Measured 2026-10-11 (last run): installing resolvconf replaced /etc/resolv.conf with its own EMPTY file, so CT 105 had no nameserver and wg-quick looped on "Temporary failure in name resolution: ch3.vpn.airdns.org:1637" for 25 minutes (the kill-switch itself was in place). Operator review 2026-10-11 of the drafted block (supersedes the earlier lists): the in-container commands are these, in this order — the base nameserver is Pi-hole on the LAN, which the kill-switch allows: `systemctl stop wg-quick@wg0 || true`; `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v4 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `echo iptables-persistent iptables-persistent/autosave_v6 boolean false | debconf-set-selections`; `apt-get update`; `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends wireguard-tools resolvconf iptables iptables-persistent`; `printf 'nameserver 192.168.1.30\n' > /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/base`; `resolvconf -u`; `chmod 600 /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf`; `iptables -F OUTPUT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d 192.168.1.0/24 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -p udp --dport 1637 -j ACCEPT`; `iptables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `ip6tables -F OUTPUT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o lo -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o wg0 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -A OUTPUT -o eth0 -d fe80::/10 -j ACCEPT`; `ip6tables -P OUTPUT DROP`; `netfilter-persistent save`; `systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0`.

Operator review 2026-10-11 of the drafted block: The draft's prerequisites are not true: measured just now, /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/base is EMPTY and /etc/resolv.conf holds no nameserver — nothing set the Pi-hole base, so re-enabling wg-quick hangs on DNS again. Do not assume earlier work; run the step's full command list from the latest review, in order, starting with `systemctl stop wg-quick@wg0 || true` and including `printf 'nameserver 192.168.1.30\n' > /etc/resolvconf/resolv.conf.d/base` and `resolvconf -u` before `systemctl enable --now wg-quick@wg0`.

Done when `pct exec 105 -- wg show` lists the wg0 peer with a recent handshake, `pct exec 105 -- curl -4 -s --max-time 15 https://api.ipify.org` prints an address that is NOT 67.240.32.243, and `pct exec 105 -- curl -6 -s --max-time 10 https://api6.ipify.org` prints nothing or the tunnel's address, never the home IPv6.
